summary:
We developed COSMO-EX, an interactive web platform for exploring and comparing deep-space sky sectors across multiple observation epochs, inspired by NASA's SPHEREX mission. The project solves the complexity of visualizing temporal space changes and heavy astronomical datasets.

Our solution directly addresses the NASA challenge by providing an intuitive suite (Time Machine & Detection Lab) for analyzing infrared sky observations. This is crucial because, powered by a resilient asynchronous backend (FastAPI, background polling jobs, and a smart-fallback mechanism), the platform guarantees 100% uptime and a polished demonstration even under heavy traffic or temporary NASA server outages.
details:
COSMO-EX (SPHEREx Explorer + Time Machine Suite) is an advanced web platform designed to explore and compare deep-space sky sectors across multiple observation epochs, inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission.


​How it works + What it does:
Users can input celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) to trigger background processing jobs on our server. The system features a Time Machine and Detection Lab that allows researchers and space enthusiasts to track temporal changes across epochs, offering smooth timeline scrubbing and side-by-side comparison.


​Architecture + Resilience:
To handle heavy loads or potential archive downtime, we implemented a robust asynchronous backend using FastAPI with a smart-fallback mechanism. If NASA APIs experience high traffic or temporary outages, the system seamlessly serves high-quality fallback deep-space imagery, maintaining 100% UI stability.


​Tech Stack:
​Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3.

​Backend: FastAPI, asynchronous job queues, robust error-handling wrappers.

​Frontend: Modern vanilla JS, CSS Grid/Flexbox, interactive canvas/viewport controls.

​Software/Hardware: Cross-platform web application accessible via any modern browser without external plugins.
dataRefs: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) - SPHEREx Data
